- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85% of recent high), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +10% above recent peak for next 3 days.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3 days, model lags in adjusting; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to forecast direction.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 5–10% for next 5 days; if below, increase by 5–10%.
- Sentiment volatility >0.5 in last 5 days correlates with forecast error; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment swings >0.5.
